description:
The panel URL preview loads ARBITRARY third-party pages (`WebviewUrl::External`), and the JS we inject into them reports the page's own title / URL / text back to the window that opened it by invoking three commands. The caller is therefore untrusted remote content, so this capability accepts any origin, and in exchange it is the narrowest capability in the app: only the three `__panel_*_report` commands, and only on `url-preview-*` webviews.

`webviews` (not `windows`) is load-bearing, and MORE so since a preview became per-window. A preview child is hosted on the app window whose page asked for it, so it can live inside `main` or inside any `window-N`. A `windows` entry naming those would enable this any-origin capability on EVERY webview of every window it named, so the scoping would invert and the previewed page would be reachable from, and reach, the app's own surface. Keep `windows` empty here forever.

The `url-preview-*` glob is the whole boundary, and the label it matches is minted from one constant, `PREVIEW_LABEL_PREFIX` in `src/panel_preview.rs`. The ACL tests build their fixtures from that same constant, so renaming the label cannot leave them green while this stops matching.

Before tauri 2.11 these calls were not ACL-checked at all (no app ACL manifest existed), which meant a previewed page could invoke ANY app command. This capability is what replaces that hole with a three-command allowlist.
